key_insight: An invariant neural-network closure brings two-equation RANS-like turbulence behavior to coarse-mesh reactor simulations without solving turbulence transport equations.
engineering_relevance: The closure improves molten-salt reactor flow predictions while retaining the low computational cost of a system thermal-hydraulics code.
method: Predict elementwise turbulent kinetic energy and timescale from neighboring flow and geometry.
Enforce translation, Galilean, rotation, reflection, and neighbor-order invariance; insert non-negative eddy viscosity into SAM’s implicit diffusive operator.
Iteratively retrain on SAM flow states against fixed Nek5000 targets to reduce coarse-mesh covariate shift.
evidence_signal: For a 120 s pump coastdown, velocity error fell from 37.6% to 17.7%, time-averaged eddy-viscosity error was 12%, and runtime was about 0.2 core-hours versus 330 for Nek5000.
watch_item: Coarse-mesh resolution still limits velocity accuracy, and transfer beyond the evaluated MSFR conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: An Invariant Neural-Network Eddy-Viscosity Closure with Iterative Solver Coupling for Molten Salt Fast Reactor Thermal-Hydraulics
